column2: Artificial Intelligence. The broader field of creating systems capable of performing tasks associated with human intelligence.
Machine Learning. A subset of AI where systems learn patterns from data rather than relying entirely on explicitly programmed rules.
Deep Learning. A subset of machine learning that uses multilayered neural networks.
A computational model composed of interconnected nodes (neurons) that process information through weighted connections.
A mathematical representation of learned patterns that accepts inputs and produces predictions or outputs.
The process of adjusting model parameters using data to improve performance on a task.
The process of using a trained model to generate predictions or outputs from new inputs.
A collection of data used for training, validation, or evaluating a model.
An individual measurable property or input variable used by a machine learning model.
The expected output or target associated with a training example.
A value learned during training, such as a neural network weight or bias.
A configuration value set outside the model's learning process, such as learning rate or batch size.
One complete pass through the entire training dataset.
A subset of training examples processed together during one training step.
A single model update or processing step, typically involving one batch.
When a model learns training data too specifically and performs poorly on unseen data.
When a model is too simple or insufficiently trained to capture important patterns.
The ability of a trained model to perform well on previously unseen data.
A collection of computational units that transform information within a neural network.
The entry point where input data is provided to a neural network.
An intermediate layer that processes representations between input and output layers.
The final layer that produces the model's prediction or output.
A computational unit that combines inputs, applies weights and biases, and typically uses an activation function.
A learned numerical value controlling the influence of one neuron on another.
A learned numerical offset added to a neuron's weighted input.
A mathematical function applied to a neuron's output to introduce nonlinearity.
Rectified Linear Unit. An activation function that returns the maximum of zero and its input.
A function that converts a set of numerical scores into a probability distribution.
A dense numerical vector representing an object, word, token, or other piece of information.
A mechanism that allows a model to dynamically determine which parts of its input are most relevant.
An attention mechanism where elements within the same sequence attend to one another.
A neural network architecture built around attention mechanisms, widely used in modern language and multimodal models.
Convolutional Neural Network. An architecture commonly used for processing images and spatial data.
Recurrent Neural Network. An architecture designed to process sequential information.
Long Short-Term Memory. A recurrent neural network architecture designed to retain information over longer sequences.
A mathematical function measuring the difference between a model's predictions and expected outputs.
The derivative of a function with respect to its parameters, indicating the direction of greatest increase.
An algorithm that calculates gradients throughout a neural network to determine how parameters should be updated.
An optimization algorithm that updates parameters in the direction that reduces the loss function.
An algorithm responsible for updating model parameters using calculated gradients.
A hyperparameter controlling the size of parameter updates during training.
An adaptive optimization algorithm combining momentum and per-parameter learning rate adjustments.
Stochastic Gradient Descent. An optimization method that updates parameters using individual examples or batches.
Techniques used to reduce overfitting and improve model generalization.
A regularization technique that randomly disables neurons during training.
Further training an existing pretrained model on a more specific dataset or task.
Reusing knowledge learned by one model to improve performance on another task.
Training a model on a large dataset before adapting it to a particular task.
Reducing the numerical precision used to represent model parameters and computations.
Removing less important model parameters or connections to reduce model size or computational requirements.
Training a smaller student model to reproduce the behavior of a larger teacher model.
Large Language Model. A neural network trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language.
A unit of text processed by a language model. It may represent a word, part of a word, punctuation, or another text unit.
A component that converts text into tokens and numerical token IDs.
The maximum amount of tokenized input and context a model can process in a single request.
The input instructions or content provided to a model.
Instructions establishing the model's behavior, role, and constraints.
Text or other output generated by a model in response to an input.
A sampling parameter controlling the randomness of generated outputs.
A sampling strategy that restricts token selection to the K most probable candidates.
A sampling strategy that selects from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches a specified threshold.
Raw, unnormalized numerical scores produced by a model before probability conversion.
Key-Value Cache. Stores previously calculated attention keys and values to avoid recomputing them during autoregressive generation.
Generating output one token at a time, using previously generated tokens as context.
A model-generated statement that is incorrect, fabricated, or unsupported by available information.
Fine-tuning a model on instruction-response examples to improve its ability to follow instructions.
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback. A training approach that uses human preferences to guide model behavior.
Low-Rank Adaptation. A parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique that introduces small trainable matrices into an existing model.
A fine-tuning technique combining quantization and LoRA to reduce memory requirements.
Mixture of Experts. An architecture that routes inputs through selected specialized subnetworks rather than activating every parameter.
Tokens used by certain models for internal reasoning or intermediate computation.
Software responsible for executing a trained model and producing outputs.
The environment and software components required to execute a model.
The numerical parameters learned during training and stored for inference.
A saved snapshot of model parameters and potentially optimizer or training state.
Open Neural Network Exchange. A format for representing machine learning models across different frameworks and runtimes.
A model file format commonly used for efficient local LLM inference, particularly with llama.cpp.
A format for storing tensor data designed to be safe and efficient to load.
NVIDIA's parallel computing platform and programming model for GPU acceleration.
AMD's GPU computing software platform.
Apple's graphics and compute API, commonly used for GPU acceleration on Apple hardware.
A cross-platform API for GPU-accelerated graphics and computation, including machine learning inference.
Processing multiple inference requests or inputs together.
Delivering generated model output incrementally rather than waiting for the complete response.
The amount of work a system processes within a given period.
The time required to complete an operation or respond to a request.
A performance measurement representing how many tokens a language model generates per second.
The amount of system memory or GPU memory required by a model and its runtime.
A model whose numerical parameters have been converted to lower precision to reduce storage and computational costs.
Running AI models directly on local devices rather than relying on remote servers.
Executing model inference locally on a device such as a phone, desktop, or embedded computer.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation. A technique that retrieves external information and supplies it to an LLM as context for generating responses.
A database designed to store and search numerical embeddings efficiently.
Finding similar items by comparing their numerical vector representations.
Searching based on meaning and conceptual similarity rather than exact keyword matches.
Splitting documents or other content into smaller sections for processing or retrieval.
A numerical measurement representing how similar two vectors or pieces of information are.
A metric measuring the angular similarity between two vectors.
An AI-driven system that can reason about tasks, select actions, and interact with tools or external systems.
Allowing a model to request execution of external functions or services.
A structured mechanism for models to request specific application functions with defined arguments.
Model Context Protocol. A protocol for connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources.
Coordinating models, tools, data sources, and workflows to complete a task.
Rules and mechanisms that constrain model inputs, outputs, and actions.
A model or system capable of processing or generating multiple types of information, such as text, images, audio, and video.
A standardized test or collection of tests used to compare model performance.
The proportion of predictions that are correct.
The proportion of positive predictions that are actually positive.
The proportion of actual positive examples that are correctly identified.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall.
A table comparing predicted classifications against actual classifications.
A metric measuring how well a language model predicts a sequence of tokens. Lower values generally indicate better predictive performance on the same evaluation data.
A dataset reserved for measuring model performance.
A dataset used during development to evaluate models and tune hyperparameters.
A dataset reserved for final evaluation of model performance.
An experiment that removes or changes components to measure their contribution to overall performance.
The ability to repeat an experiment and obtain consistent results under equivalent conditions.
Accelerating generation by using a smaller draft model to propose tokens for verification by a larger model.
Dynamically combining incoming inference requests into GPU batches.
A memory-management approach for efficiently handling attention KV caches.
An optimized attention algorithm that reduces memory traffic.
A tensor library and associated ecosystem underlying various local inference implementations.
Single Instruction, Multiple Data. CPU instructions that operate on multiple data elements simultaneously.
16-bit floating-point numerical representation.
Brain Floating Point 16-bit representation, with a wider exponent range than FP16.
8-bit integer representation frequently used for quantized inference.
4-bit integer representation used to substantially reduce model storage requirements.
Making a model available to applications through an inference interface.
The initial startup cost of loading and initializing a model.
Processing the input prompt before autoregressive token generation begins.
The autoregressive generation phase that produces output tokens.
